questions.prompt: The displayed fictional excerpt says 'The bus arrived late twice this week.' The candidate presents 'The bus never arrived this week' as an exact quote. What is the safest classification?

options.label: A
options.text: Accept because both sentences concern a bus.

options.label: B
options.text: Treat it only as contextual disagreement and record no error.

options.label: C
options.text: Flag fabricated_or_altered_quote, locate the candidate_quote, and do not accept.

questions.prompt: One fictional speaker says an evening service helped after work; another says evening care duties still prevented attendance. A candidate explicitly preserves both accounts and claims the schedule worked differently across speakers. What follows?

options.label: A
options.text: Any disagreement makes the interpretation insufficiently warranted.

options.label: B
options.text: Disagreement is not itself a defect when both accounts warrant the bounded claim and remain visible.

options.label: C
options.text: Remove the less common account so the theme is more coherent.
